AiCostBreakdown.description: Requests, tokens and USD cost for one slice (text or vision) of recorded AI usage.

costUsd.description: Cost in USD, recomputed from the tokens above at this report's per-token prices. Six decimal places: a single call costs far less than a cent.

inputTokens.description: Prompt tokens summed over the slice.

outputTokens.description: Completion tokens summed over the slice.

requests.description: Metered requests in the slice, including failed ones.

AiCostByPlanItem.description: Cost to serve one plan over the reporting period.

activeUsers.description: Distinct users on this plan with recorded usage in the period. Users who made no AI call are not counted — they cost nothing to serve.

costPerActiveUserUsd.description: `totalCostUsd` divided by `activeUsers`; zero when nobody was active. Compare this against the plan's price to read the margin.

text.description: Text-only calls: chat, insights, summaries, category suggestions.

vision.description: Vision calls: receipt analysis. Usually the smaller request count and the larger bill.

AiCostByUserItem.description: Cost to serve one user over the reporting period.

plan.description: The plan the user is on now — `FREE`, `PREMIUM` or `TRIAL`. This is the plan at report time, not necessarily the plan held during the period.

text.description: Text-only calls: chat, insights, summaries, category suggestions.

AiCostPricing.description: The per-token prices used to compute this report, and when they were last checked.

pricesLastCheckedOn.description: The date a human last reconciled these rates against the provider's published pricing. Treat the report as an estimate that ages from this date.

textInputPerMtokUsd.description: USD per million prompt tokens for text calls.

textOutputPerMtokUsd.description: USD per million completion tokens for text calls.

visionInputPerMtokUsd.description: USD per million prompt tokens for vision (receipt) calls. An order of magnitude above the text rate — an image is billed as a large token block.

visionOutputPerMtokUsd.description: USD per million completion tokens for vision (receipt) calls.

AiCostReport.description: Cost to serve per user and per plan, recomputed from recorded AI usage.

byPlan.description: Every plan with recorded usage in the period.

byUser.description: Every user with recorded usage in the period, most expensive first.

periodEnd.description: Last day counted, inclusive, in Asia/Manila.

periodStart.description: First day counted, inclusive, in Asia/Manila.

pricing.description: The per-token prices used, and when they were last checked.

AlertChatItem.description: An alert in a chat answer — enough to render the notice and mark it read.

id.description: Stable alert identifier. Pass it back to mark read, dismiss or delete.

message.description: The human-readable notice, already composed by the server.
message.example: You have used 92% of your Groceries budget for August.

read.description: Whether the user has already seen this alert.

AlertChatItemList.description: The result of a `list_alerts` turn: a JSON array of alerts.

BudgetChatItem.description: One category's budget line in a chat budget summary.

budgeted.description: The budget limit for the month, in PHP.

percentUsed.description: Share of the budget used, as a percentage. May exceed 100.

remaining.description: `budgeted` minus `spent`, in PHP. Negative once the budget is exceeded.

spent.description: Spent against this budget so far, in PHP.

status.description: Banding derived from `percentUsed`: `WARNING` at 80%, `OVER_BUDGET` at 100%. The server computes it — a client must never re-derive it.

BudgetSummaryChatResult.description: A month's budget summary as returned by a chat turn.

items.description: One line per budgeted category. Empty when no budget is set.

safeToSpend.description: What remains across all budgets for the month, in PHP.

totalBudgeted.description: Sum of every budget limit for the month, in PHP.

totalSpent.description: Sum of spending against those budgets, in PHP.

BulkDeleteChatResult.description: How many expenses a bulk delete actually removed.

deleted.description: The number of expenses deleted. Can be lower than the number asked for — ids that no longer exist are skipped rather than failing the turn — and can be zero when a filter matched nothing.

CategoryResponseList.description: The result of a `list_categories` turn: a JSON array of the user's categories, as full CategoryResponse records.

CategoryTotalChatItem.description: A category and what was spent in it over the requested window.

total.description: Total spent in this category, in PHP, rounded to two decimal places.

CategoryTotalChatItemList.description: The result of a `get_category_totals` turn: a JSON array of category totals.

ChatConfirmRequest.description: A confirmation of a previously previewed action. Echo the preview's `toolName` and `params` back unchanged.

conversationId.description: The conversation the confirmed turn belongs to, so it is recorded in the same transcript as the preview. Omit to start a new conversation.

mode.description: `force` re-runs a create that was held back by the duplicate check (the user chose "add anyway"). Anything else, including omitting it, executes with the duplicate check still on.

params.description: The tool's arguments, copied from the preview's `params` unchanged. The key set varies by tool and is not part of this contract.

toolName.description: The tool to run, copied from the preview's `toolName`. An unknown tool is rejected with 400 rather than answered as prose.

ChatPreviewData.description: A pending assistant action awaiting confirmation. Echo `toolName` and `params` back to POST /ai/chat/confirm; the client never interprets them, it only renders and returns them.

existingId.description: The id of the expense this one looks like a duplicate of. Present only on the duplicate-confirmation turn, which arrives as `type: "disambiguate"` rather than `"preview"`; the property is omitted, not null, on every other turn. A client may show it to let the user open the existing row before confirming.

params.description: The tool's arguments, exactly as the assistant produced them. The key set varies by tool and is not part of this contract — treat it as opaque.

toolName.description: The tool the assistant resolved, e.g. `create_expense`. This is the one field that says which action is pending.

ChatResponse.description: One assistant turn: what kind of turn it is, what to say, and an optional structured payload to render.

conversationId.description: The conversation this turn belongs to. Omitted — not null — on turns served before a conversation is established, such as the circuit-breaker fallback.

message.description: The assistant's reply, ready to render. Always present, and always sufficient on its own — a client that cannot render `result` can show this.

result.description: The structured payload for this turn, omitted when the turn carries none. Which member applies follows from the tool the assistant ran, which is not itself on the wire — so narrow on `type` first, then on the payload's own properties. See TEN-275 for why an explicit per-payload discriminator is not published here.

type.description: The turn's kind, and the only field a client should branch on before reading `result`. `text` — prose only, no payload. `action` — something was read or written; `result` carries it. `preview` — a write is pending confirmation and `result` is a ChatPreviewData. `disambiguate` — the assistant needs the user to choose before it proceeds.

ConversationSummaryDto.description: A chat conversation as it appears in a history list — enough to render a row and fetch the transcript, without the messages themselves.

createdAt.description: When the conversation was started. ISO-8601 local date-time, no offset.

id.description: Stable identifier. Pass it to GET /chat/conversations/{id} for the transcript.

title.description: The conversation's first user message, trimmed to 60 characters. Null until the first turn is recorded — a conversation can exist with no messages, so a history list must render a placeholder rather than assume a label.
title.example: How much did I spend on groceries?

updatedAt.description: When the last turn was recorded. The list is ordered by this field, newest first, so it is also the sort key a client should display.

ExpenseChatItem.description: An expense in a chat answer — flattened for a chat bubble.

amount.description: Amount in PHP, rounded to two decimal places for display.

category.description: Category name, or the literal `Uncategorized` when the expense has no category. Never null.

date.description: The expense date as `YYYY-MM-DD` in Asia/Manila, or an empty string on the rare rows with no date. Not declared as a date format for that reason — parse defensively.

ExpenseChatItemList.description: The result of a `search_expenses` turn: a JSON array of matching expenses, at most 50.

ExpenseDisambiguateItem.description: One expense the user must choose between before a delete can proceed.

amount.description: Amount in PHP, at the stored precision. Unlike ExpenseChatItem this is not rounded for display, so format it at the edge.

date.description: The expense date as `YYYY-MM-DD` in Asia/Manila, or an empty string on the rare rows with no date.

description.description: What the expense was for — the field the user's ambiguous phrase matched.

id.description: The expense's identifier. Send it back to name the one to delete.

ExpenseDisambiguateItemList.description: The result of a delete-expense `disambiguate` turn: a JSON array of the candidates the user must choose between.

source.description: How this expense was created. Only MANUAL and RECEIPT_SCAN may be declared by a client — the other values belong to routes that write the row themselves, and naming one here is rejected with 400. Omitted means MANUAL. Ignored on update: a source is recorded once, at creation.

How this expense was created. Only MANUAL and RECEIPT_SCAN may be declared by a client — the other values belong to routes that write the row themselves, and naming one here is rejected with 400. Omitted means MANUAL. Ignored on update: a source is recorded once, at creation.
The route that created this expense. Rows written before the field existed report MANUAL.

GoalChatItem.description: A savings goal in a chat answer — the subset a chat bubble renders.

progressPercent.description: Progress as a percentage, 0–100. Not money: a decimal fraction here is correct.

savedAmount.description: Amount saved so far, in PHP.

status.description: Where the goal stands against its target date.

targetAmount.description: Target amount in PHP, at full decimal precision.

targetDate.description: Target date as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Absent — the property is omitted, not null — when the goal has no target date.

GoalChatItemList.description: The result of a `list_goals` turn: a JSON array of savings goals.

MonthlyReportChatResult.description: A month's spending report as returned by a chat turn.

categoryBreakdown.description: Spend per category for the month. Empty when nothing was spent.

topExpenses.description: The month's five largest expenses, descending by amount. Fewer than five when the month has fewer expenses.

totalSpent.description: Total spent in the month, in PHP. Equals the sum of `categoryBreakdown[].total`; the server computes it, a client must not re-derive it.

RecategorizeChatResult.description: How many expenses a bulk recategorization moved.

updated.description: The number of expenses moved to the target category. Zero when nothing matched the source category over the requested window.

RecurringChatItem.description: A recurring expense in a chat answer.

active.description: False once paused; a paused entry is still listed, but generates nothing and never appears in `upcoming`.

amount.description: Amount charged each period, in PHP.

categoryName.description: Category the generated expenses land in.

RecurringChatResult.description: A user's recurring expenses and the bills due this month.

items.description: Every recurring expense the user has, active or paused.

upcoming.description: Bills falling due in the requested month. A projection of `items`, not a parallel list — the two can differ in length, and a paused entry appears in `items` only.

SubscriptionChatResult.description: The user's plan and what it entitles them to, as reported by a chat turn.

admin.description: True when the account is an administrator, which bypasses plan gating and AI quota entirely.

features.description: The capabilities currently unlocked. Unordered, and already resolved against `status` — a client gates on membership here, never on `plan`.

plan.description: The tier in force. `FREE` is the implicit default when there is no active subscription.

status.description: The subscription's lifecycle state. Only `ACTIVE` and `TRIAL` grant a paid plan's features — the other values mean the effective plan is `FREE`.

UpcomingBillChatItem.description: A bill projected to fall due in the requested month.

dueDate.description: The due date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, in Asia/Manila.

bearerAuth.description: Backend-issued JWT from POST /auth/login, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

get.description: Recomputes USD cost from recorded token counts, keeping text and vision apart, and states the per-token prices used and when they were last checked. Defaults to month-to-date in Asia/Manila.
get.summary: Cost to serve per user and per plan

post.description: Runs the action the server proposed on a `preview` turn. Post that turn's `toolName` and `params` back unchanged; no natural language is sent, so nothing is re-parsed and the executed action is the one that was shown.
post.summary: Execute a previously previewed assistant action

get.description: Conversation summaries for the authenticated user, most recently updated first. Carries no messages; fetch a transcript with GET /chat/conversations/{id}.

200.description: The caller's conversations, newest activity first. Empty when they have never chatted.
